title: Cartesian and simplicial compatibility of the Reedy model on simplicial spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and their Kan model structure from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the model-category axioms and Reedy structure from [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Work in fixed universes, enlarged if needed, in $\mathrm{sS}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{sSet})$ with the Reedy model structure. A monomorphism is a map injective in every bidegree. Put $F(n)_k=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([k],[n])$, discrete in the inner direction, and let $cK$ be the constant simplicial space on a simplicial set $K$. Define $\operatorname{Map}(A,X)_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sS}}(A\times c\Delta^q,X)$, with operators by precomposition. The cartesian internal hom is $(X^A)_{n,q}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sS}}(A\times F(n)\times c\Delta^q,X)$.

The Reedy cofibrations are precisely the monomorphisms. For Reedy cofibrations $i:A\to B$ and $j:C\to D$, the map
$$(A\times D)\amalg_{A\times C}(B\times C)\longrightarrow B\times D$$
is a Reedy cofibration, and it is a Reedy weak equivalence if either $i$ or $j$ is a Reedy weak equivalence. Moreover, for a Reedy cofibration $i:A\to B$ and a Reedy fibration $p:X\to Y$, the canonical map
$$\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$$
is a Kan fibration, trivial if either $i$ or $p$ is a Reedy weak equivalence.

source.place: Rezk, A model for the homotopy theory of homotopy theory, Sections 2.3-2.5, printed pp. 6-7; in particular the Reedy cartesian-compatibility assertion at the end of 2.5. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-space result.

proof.text: Identify the latching object in outer degree $n$. For a fixed inner degree $q$, a representative of $(L_nX)_q$ is a pair $(\sigma,z)$ with $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[k]$, $k<n$, and $z\in X_{k,q}$; its image in $X_{n,q}$ is $\sigma^*z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to the outer simplicial set $m\mapsto X_{m,q}$. If $z=\tau^*y$ is its unique nondegenerate decomposition, the latching-colimit relation identifies $(\sigma,z)$ with $(\tau\sigma,y)$. Two representatives with the same image have the same nondegenerate simplex and composite surjection by uniqueness, so they are identified with this same representative. Thus $(L_nX)_q\to X_{n,q}$ is injective with image $D_nX_q$, the union of all proper outer-degeneracy images. Inner operators preserve this subset because they commute with outer degeneracies. These identifications therefore give $L_nX\cong D_nX\subseteq X_n$ as simplicial sets. At $n=0$ the indexing category and $D_0X$ are both empty. The colimit description is precisely the latching definition of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure].

source.place: Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets; application degree by degree to the Reedy latching colimit of Rezk Section 2.4.

proof.text: A Reedy cofibration is objectwise a cofibration by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], hence injective in each bidegree by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Conversely identify a bidegree monomorphism $A\to B$ with its image. Then $A_n\cap D_nB=D_nA$: if $a\in A_{n,q}$ equals $\sigma^*b$ in $B$ for a proper surjection $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[k]$, take the order-preserving section $\delta(t)=\min\sigma^{-1}(t)$, so $\sigma\delta=1_{[k]}$, and compute $b=\delta^*a\in A_{k,q}$. Using step 1, the relative latching map is consequently the inclusion $A_n\cup D_nB\hookrightarrow B_n$. It is a Kan-model cofibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The relative-latching criterion in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] now proves that $A\to B$ is a Reedy cofibration. This includes $n=0$, where the relative latching map is $A_0\to B_0$.

source.place: Section 2.4, printed p. 6: cofibrations are inclusions; expanded relative-latching argument.

proof.text: Write $i\mathbin{\square}j$ for the pushout-product map in the statement. By step 2 identify $A$ with a subobject of $B$ and $C$ with a subobject of $D$. At every bidegree the two subsets $A\times D$ and $B\times C$ of $B\times D$ intersect in $A\times C$. Their pushout is their union: its elements are those in either subset, with the two copies of each element of the intersection identified. All outer and inner operators preserve these identifications, so this is also the pushout simplicial space. Its inclusion in $B\times D$ is injective in each bidegree and hence a Reedy cofibration by step 2.

source.place: Section 2.5, printed p. 7, assertion (1), cofibration part; explicit degreewise union calculation.

proof.text: Suppose that $j$ is also a Reedy weak equivalence. By [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], each $j_n$ is a weak homotopy equivalence; it is a monomorphism by step 2. It is therefore a trivial cofibration in the Kan model of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. By the weak-factorization-system characterization of a model category in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], this says exactly that $j_n$ has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration, namely that it is anodyne in the terminology of [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. That node applied to the monomorphism $i_n$ and the anodyne map $j_n$ makes $(i\mathbin{\square}j)_n=i_n\mathbin{\square}j_n$ anodyne, hence a Kan trivial cofibration by the same model-category characterization. In particular it is a weak homotopy equivalence. This holds for every $n$, giving a Reedy weak equivalence. If instead $i$ is a Reedy weak equivalence, $i_n$ is a monomorphism and a weak homotopy equivalence, hence a Kan trivial cofibration and therefore anodyne by that weak-factorization-system characterization. Apply [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] to the monomorphism $j_n$ and the anodyne map $i_n$. It makes $j_n\mathbin{\square}i_n$ anodyne and thus a Kan trivial cofibration. The coordinate flip $(b,d)\mapsto(d,b)$ restricts from $B_n\times D_n$ to the two pushout pieces, taking $A_n\times D_n$ to $D_n\times A_n$ and $B_n\times C_n$ to $C_n\times B_n$, with their intersection taken to $C_n\times A_n$. It therefore identifies $i_n\mathbin{\square}j_n$ with this anodyne map. Hence $(i\mathbin{\square}j)_n$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $n$, as required.

source.place: Section 2.5, printed p. 7, assertion (1), weak-equivalence part; the underlying simplicial-set theorem is the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text:
Spell out the adjunction used for lifting. A map $f:T\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)$ is a family $h_t:A\times c\Delta^q\to X$, indexed by $t\in T_q$, with $h_{T(\theta)t}=h_t\circ(1_A\times c\Delta(\theta))$ for $\theta:[r]\to[q]$. Define $g_{n,q}(a,t)=(h_t)_{n,q}(a,1_{[q]})$ for $a\in A_{n,q}$. Naturality of $h_t$ and the displayed family identity give $X(\alpha,\beta)g_{n,q}(a,t)=g_{k,r}(A(\alpha,\beta)a,T(\beta)t)$ for $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ and $\beta:[r]\to[q]$, so $g:A\times cT\to X$ is a map. Conversely, given $g$, set $(h_t)_{n,r}(a,\theta)=g_{n,r}(a,T(\theta)t)$. Functoriality $T(\theta\gamma)=T(\gamma)T(\theta)$ and naturality of $g$ verify the family identity and naturality of each $h_t$. Evaluating at the identity recovers $g$; in the other direction the family identity gives $(h_{T(\theta)t})_{n,r}(a,1_{[r]})=(h_t)_{n,r}(a,\theta)$ and recovers every value of $h_t$. This proves the natural tensor-mapping adjunction for every $T$.

For the internal hom formula in the statement, let $g:C\times A\to X$. For $c\in C_{n,q}$ define $h_c:A\times F(n)\times c\Delta^q\to X$ by $(h_c)_{k,r}(a,\alpha,\beta)=g_{k,r}(C(\alpha,\beta)c,a)$, where $a\in A_{k,r}$, $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ and $\beta:[r]\to[q]$. Naturality of $g$ shows that this is a map and that the family is a map $C\to X^A$. Conversely, from such a family define $g_{n,q}(c,a)=(h_c)_{n,q}(a,1_{[n]},1_{[q]})$. Compatibility of the family with both representable coordinates states $(h_{C(\alpha,\beta)c})_{k,r}(a,1_{[k]},1_{[r]})=(h_c)_{k,r}(a,\alpha,\beta)$. Thus reconstruction recovers every $h_c$, while evaluation of the family constructed from $g$ returns $g(c,a)$. Naturality of $h_c$ and this identity also make the reconstructed $g$ natural in both indices. This proves the asserted internal hom formula.

Put $r:\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$. For $u:S\to T$, the tensor-mapping adjunction identifies a square $u$ against $r$ with maps $B\times cS\to X$ and $A\times cT\to X$ agreeing on $A\times cS$, over the given map $B\times cT\to Y$. Their union is the map from the pushout domain of $i\mathbin{\square}cu$, so this is a square $i\mathbin{\square}cu$ against $p$. A filler $B\times cT\to X$ is precisely a map $T\to\operatorname{Map}(B,X)$ with the two prescribed restrictions, proving the filler correspondence.

source.place: Section 2.3, printed pp. 5-6, enrichment and internal hom; Section 2.5: pushout-product/lifting adjunction, with evaluation formulas.

proof.text: Let $u:\Lambda_t^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$, be any horn inclusion. It is a Kan trivial cofibration: it is a one-cell horn attachment in the characterization of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Consequently $cu$ is a bidegree monomorphism and an objectwise weak equivalence; step 2 and [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] make it a Reedy trivial cofibration. Steps 3-4 make $i\mathbin{\square}cu$ a Reedy trivial cofibration. Since $p$ is a Reedy fibration, the model lifting axiom of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] supplies a filler against $p$. Step 5 gives a filler for $u$ against $r$. This works for all horns, so $r$ is a Kan fibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. No fibrancy hypothesis on $X$ or $Y$ separately has been used.

source.place: Sections 2.4-2.5, printed pp. 6-7: simplicial model compatibility; horn-lifting verification.

proof.text: Finally take $u:\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ for every $m\geq0$. Its constant extension is a monomorphism, hence a Reedy cofibration by step 2. If $i$ is a Reedy weak equivalence, steps 3-4 make $i\mathbin{\square}cu$ a Reedy trivial cofibration and the Reedy fibration $p$ lifts against it. If $p$ is a Reedy weak equivalence, it is a Reedy trivial fibration and lifts against the Reedy cofibration $i\mathbin{\square}cu$ from step 3. Both lifting assertions are the weak-factorization-system axioms stated in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. In either case step 5 supplies a filler for every boundary against $r$. The boundary characterization of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], including $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$, makes $r$ a trivial Kan fibration. This proves both requested triviality cases.

source.place: Sections 2.4-2.5, printed pp. 6-7: triviality in the simplicial mapping axiom; boundary-lifting verification including degree zero.

lean.statement: theorem reedy_cartesian_simplicial : (∀ (A B : SimplicialSpace.{u}) (i : A ⟶ B), IsReedyCofibration i ↔ ∀ n q : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Injective ((i.app n).app q)) ∧ (∀ (A B C D : SimplicialSpace.{u}) (i : A ⟶ B) (j : C ⟶ D), IsReedyCofibration i → IsReedyCofibration j → IsReedyCofibration (((CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.Arrow.pushoutProduct.obj (Arrow.mk i)).obj (Arrow.mk j)).hom) ∧ ((IsReedyWeakEquivalence i ∨ IsReedyWeakEquivalence j) → IsReedyWeakEquivalence (((CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.Arrow.pushoutProduct.obj (Arrow.mk i)).obj (Arrow.mk j)).hom))) ∧ (∀ (A B X Y : SimplicialSpace.{u}) (i : A ⟶ B) (p : X ⟶ Y), IsReedyCofibration i → IsReedyFibration p → Fibration (mappingPullback i p) ∧ ((IsReedyWeakEquivalence i ∨ IsReedyWeakEquivalence p) → Fibration (mappingPullback i p) ∧ Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (mappingPullback i p)))
lean.note: Uses the recorded Reedy relative-latching and relative-matching classes, Kan fibrations, and realization-based weak equivalences. Reuses SimplicialSpace, constant, discreteRepresentable, the cartesian closed instance and IsReedyFibration already published in SegalCartesianExponent; no use of its downstream cartesian_exponent theorem. The mapping space is the degree-zero internal hom, whose simplices are the specified maps by adjunction and Yoneda. The mapping pullback is the canonical pullback lift, with commutativity supplied by internal-hom naturality.
